description: Athlete asks for a lighter week due to work stress. Dean should reduce this week's volume temporarily and give a concrete adjusted plan — without treating it as a permanent change or skipping quality entirely.
inbound_sms: Work has been brutal this week, I'm exhausted. Can we dial it back? Maybe just 3 easy runs

user.name: Marcus
user.experience_level: experienced — running 6 years, marathon PR 3:28, targeting sub-3:20

ground_truth.expected_change: Reduce this week to ~3 easy runs as requested. Drop the interval workout and shorten or drop the long run. This week becomes an ad hoc recovery week.
ground_truth.change_scope: This week only. Next week resumes normal plan.
must_include: acknowledgment that next week picks back up normally
validation that this is the right call when exhausted
must_not_include: insisting Marcus must keep the interval workout or tempo
treating this as a permanent restructure of the whole plan
total week mileage exceeding ~25mi given 3 easy runs + already-logged 8mi
ground_truth.tradeoff_to_flag: Missing one big build week is fine this far out. Dean should reassure without over-explaining.
ground_truth.notes: Rest and stress-driven load reduction is legitimate coaching. Dean should be supportive, give 3 specific easy run days with distances, confirm next week resumes. Keep it short — this doesn't need a dissertation. Do NOT prescribe a quality session when the athlete asked for easy runs only.
